newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sterling drifts lower as Labour wins in landslide.
newsitem.headline: Sterling drifts lower as Labour wins in landslide.

text.p: Sterling drifted lower in thin Asian trade on Friday as the mammoth scale of Labour's win in the British general election began to prompt some nervous selling, dealers said.
At 0135 gmt sterling was quoted at 2.7950/60 marks while cable was at 1.6225/35.
Sterling had initially rallied to 2.8010/20 and 1.6290/6300 respectively just after exit polls had predicted a Labour win.
At 0136 GMT the British Broadcasting Corporation estimated Labour would have a majority over the Conservatives of 177 parliamentary seats.
"The rally on the exit polls was a knee-jerk reaction, one of relief that we weren't going to get a hung parliament," a trader at a European bank in Singapore said.
However, he added, "Because it's such a large majority it means Labour can do what they like. But what does that mean? No-one really knows."
The head of Treasury at another European bank in Singapore commented, "We've got rid of one uncertainty (the result) and now we've got more."

"It looks like a monster landslide. I've just seen on Reuters there are fears of unchecked power. Right enough. They can do whatever they want to do and they've had no practice of doing it," he added.
However, he added, "I can't see them going in and being silly. At least certainly not in the first few months."

He said the market would be very interested to learn whether or not Labour's expected Chancellor of the Exchequer (Finance Minister) Gordon Brown would be holding a meeting with the Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
A meeting is scheduled to be held next week, but there has been some market speculation it may be postponed.
"Any uncertainty over the relationship between the new Chancellor and the Governor would defintely hurt sterling," he said.

He said he still favours the scenario of an upward move in U.K. interest rates pretty soon. British bank base rates are at six percent but futures prices indicate the market expects a 1/2 point rise within the next few months.
The head of trading at a U.S. bank in Singapore said he was encouraged by comments made by Gordon Brown to Reuters Financial Television early on Friday.
Brown told RFTV a Labour government would stick to an inflation target of 2.5 percent and would set monetary policy to meet it.
"I take those as bullish comments and have bought some sterling," he said.
"I think you should buy sterling on the dips because of the interest rate scenario. And you can't ignore such fundamentals as economic growth and inflation," he added.
"Some people are scared that the left wing (of the Labour Party) will rear its ugly head -- I doubt it," he said.
He said he expected sterling to remain within its recent trading range against the mark of 2.7800/8250 for the time being.
"I get the impression Blair is more conservative than Major," he added.
